intro.title: CSS Modules
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Vue component that uses CSS Modules to style a button and a heading. You will learn how CSS Modules work by scoping CSS class names locally to a component, preventing style conflicts. The main technologies involved are Vue single-file components (.vue files) and the `module` attribute on `<style>` tags. By the end, you'll understand how to import and apply scoped CSS classes in your template using Vue's `$style` object.
intro.usecase: CSS Modules are essential in large-scale Vue applications where component reuse and style isolation prevent conflicts. In enterprise dashboards with multiple interactive panels like data charts, filters, and modals, each component needs encapsulated styles to avoid unintended overrides. E-commerce product pages with dynamic UI elements such as size selectors, color pickers, and recommendation carousels rely on CSS Modules to maintain consistent, conflict-free styling. This approach is also critical in design systems where reusable UI components must function predictably across different sections of an application without global CSS collisions.
